nodes.title: Perfectoid Hebbarkeitssatz in characteristic p: almost sections of O+/t off a Zariski closed subset
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic p, 0 != t in m_K, (R, R+) a perfectoid affinoid K-algebra, X = Spa(R, R+), I in R an ideal with I+ = I cap R+ and Z = V(I). Then there is an isomorphism of almost O_K-modules Hom_{R+}(I^{+1/p^infty}, R+/t)^a = H^0(X \ Z, O_X^+/t)^a, compatible with evaluation at every x in X \ Z (Proposition 2.3.2). For a map R -> R' of perfectoid K-algebras and I' = IR', the map I^{+1/p^infty} (x)_{R+} R'^+ -> I'^{+1/p^infty} is an almost isomorphism (Lemma 2.3.4).
hypotheses: K perfectoid of characteristic p; t a nonzero element of m_K, so m_K is the union of t^{1/p^n} O_K.
(R, R+) perfectoid affinoid; I an arbitrary ideal (the proof filters by finitely generated submodules and inducts on the number of generators).
Almost mathematics is with respect to m_K; Lemma 2.3.1 (stalk of O+/t at x is k(x)+/t) holds on any adic space over a nonarchimedean field.
proofSteps: Lemma 2.3.1: the stalk of O_X^+/t at x is k(x)+/t, because a germ f vanishing at x becomes divisible by t on the neighbourhood |f| <= |t|.

Principal case I = (f), f in R+: show I^{+1/p^infty} is almost f^{1/p^infty} R+; cover X \ V(f) by the rational sets U_n = {|f| >= |t|^n} and use [52, Lemma 6.4(i)] to write H^0(U_n, O+/t)^a as (R+/t[u_n^{1/p^infty}]/(u_n^{1/p^m} f^{1/p^m} - t^{n/p^m}))^a.

Compare the inverse systems S_n^(k) (generated by u_n^i, i <= 1/p^k) with im(R+/t -> S_n) via multiplication by f^{1/p^k}; kernels and cokernels are killed by t^{n/p^k}, and the kernel of R+/t -> im(R+/t -> S_n) is Mittag-Leffler zero along the cofinal indices n = p^{k+1}.
Identify lim_k R+/t (transition maps multiplication by f^{1/p^k - 1/p^k'}) with Hom_{R+}(f^{1/p^infty} R+, R+/t) using perfectness of R+ to show the colimit M -> f^{1/p^infty} R+ is injective.

General case: X \ V(I1 + I2) is the union of X \ V(I1) and X \ V(I2) with intersection X \ V(I1 I2); use the sheaf property and the almost exact sequence 0 -> (I1 I2)^{+1/p^infty} -> I1^{+1/p^infty} (+) I2^{+1/p^infty} -> (I1 + I2)^{+1/p^infty} -> 0, then apply Hom_{R+}(-, R+/t)^a.
Lemma 2.3.4: reduce to I principal; I^{+1/p^infty} is almost the colimit of R+ along multiplication by f^{1/p^k - 1/p^{k+1}}, which commutes with base change.
acceptance: For I = R (Z empty) both sides are (R+/t)^a by [52, Th. 6.3(iii),(iv)] (Remark 2.3.3).
Remark 2.3.3: for x outside Z the image of I+ in O_{k(x)} is almost everything, so evaluation lands in O^a_{k(x)}/t; the map is pinned down by injectivity of H^0 into the product of stalks.

nodes.title: Hebbarkeitssatz on a Hasse-invariant locus of a perfected normal F_p-variety admitting a resolution
nodes.statement: Let A0 be normal, integral and of finite type over F_p, 0 != f in A0, K = F_p((t^{1/p^infty})), S = A0^{1/p^infty} (x)^_{F_p} K with S+ = S° , Y = Spa(S, S+), X = {y in Y : |f(y)| >= |t|} with (R, R+) = (O_Y(X), O_Y^+(X)), 0 != I0 in A0, I = I0 R and Z = V(I). If Spec A0 admits a resolution of singularities (a proper birational T -> Spec A0 with T smooth over F_p), then H^0(X, O_X^+/t)^a -> H^0(X \ Z, O_X^+/t)^a is an isomorphism of almost O_K-modules (Corollary 2.3.5). Its key input is Lemma 2.3.6: for 0 != f, g in A0 the maps A0^{1/p^infty} -> Hom(g^{1/p^infty} A0^{1/p^infty}, A0^{1/p^infty}) and A0^{1/p^infty}/f -> Hom(g^{1/p^infty} A0^{1/p^infty}, A0^{1/p^infty}/f) are almost isomorphisms for the ideal generated by all f^{1/p^m}.
hypotheses: A0 normal, integral, of finite type over F_p; f and g nonzero.

Resolution of singularities of Spec A0 is assumed; Remark 2.3.7: without it the first map of Lemma 2.3.6 is an isomorphism and the second is injective, resolution being needed only for almost surjectivity of the second.

In the application Spec A0 is an open subset of the minimal compactification of the Siegel moduli space in characteristic p, f is the Hasse invariant and I0 the boundary ideal; the resolution is supplied by a toroidal compactification (Lemma 3.2.27, citing [28]).
proofSteps: Reduce as in Proposition 2.3.2 to I generated by one element g in A0.

Rewrite R+a/t as A0^{1/p^infty}[u^{1/p^infty}]/(uf)^a with almost structure given by (u^{1/p^infty} f^{1/p^infty}), and Hom_{R+}(g^{1/p^infty} R+, R+/t)^a as Hom over A0^{1/p^infty} into A; the kernel of g^{1/p^infty} A0^{1/p^infty} (x) A -> g^{1/p^infty} A is almost zero.
Using the decomposition of A into copies of A0^{1/p^infty} u^i (0 <= i < 1) and A0^{1/p^infty}/f u^i (i >= 1), reduce to Lemma 2.3.6.
Lemma 2.3.6, first map: injectivity because A0^{1/p^infty} is a domain; surjectivity by checking rank-one valuations on the normal noetherian A0.

Lemma 2.3.6, second map, A0 smooth: A0^{1/p^infty} is flat over A0; Krull intersection gives the intersection over n of (f, g^{1-1/p^n}) A0^{1/p^infty} equal to (f, g) A0^{1/p^infty}; compute Hom via an inverse limit with R^1 lim term M and show ker(f: M -> M) is killed by all f^{1/p^n} using valuations v_i at the generic points of V(f) and a constant C with v_i(g) <= C.
General A0: pull back to a resolution T; Zariski's main theorem pi_* O_T = O, coherence of R^1 pi_* O_T bounds f-power torsion, giving almost isomorphisms after passing to perfections and adjunction.
acceptance: Application check (Lemma 3.2.27): A0 an affine open of X* (x) F_p for the Siegel minimal compactification, f = Ha, I0 the boundary ideal; the resolution is a toroidal compactification.
Smooth test: A0 = F_p[x, y], f = y, I0 = (x, y); the statement reduces to the smooth case of Lemma 2.3.6.

nodes.title: Good triples (X, Z, U): Hebbarkeitssatz for the Hasse blow-up, finite normal covers and inverse limits
nodes.statement: Definition 2.3.8: for a perfectoid field K and 0 != t in K with |p| <= |t| < 1, a triple (X, Z, U) of an affinoid perfectoid X over K, a closed Z in X and a quasi-compact open U in X \ Z is good if H^0(X, O+/t)^a = H^0(X \ Z, O+/t)^a injects into H^0(U, O+/t)^a; this is independent of t, compatible with tilting, and then holds for every t in O_K including t = 0 (bounded functions extend uniquely from X \ Z to X). Lemma 2.3.9: if A0 is normal of finite type over F_p admitting a resolution of singularities, R0 = (A0 (x)^ K)<u>/(uf - t) with f in A0 not a zero-divisor, I0 = J R0 with V(J) of codimension >= 2 in Spec A0, U0 = {|g| = 1 for some g in J} and K = F_p((t^{1/p^infty})), then the perfected triple (X, Z, U) is good. Lemma 2.3.10: if (X, Z, U) is good, R0 is normal, V(I0) has codimension >= 2, and R0' is a finite normal R0-algebra etale outside V(I0) with no irreducible component of Spec R0' mapping into V(I0), then the trace pairing is perfect on R0', almost perfect on the perfected integral rings, H^0(V', O+/t)^a = Hom_{R°/t}(R'°/t, H^0(V, O+/t))^a for opens V with preimage V', the pulled back triple (X', Z', U') is good, and if X' -> X is surjective then H^0(X, O+/t) -> H^0(X', O+/t) cap H^0(U, O+/t) is an almost isomorphism. Lemma 2.3.11: for a filtered inductive system of such R0^(i) with surjective transition maps X^(i) -> X^(j), the limit triple (X~, Z~, U~) is good. Corollary 2.3.12: Lemma 2.3.9 holds for K the completion of an algebraic extension of F_p((t^{1/p^infty})).
hypotheses: Lemmas 2.3.9-2.3.11 are in characteristic p: R0 a reduced Tate K-algebra topologically of finite type, R its completed perfection, X = Spa(R, R°).

Codimension >= 2 of the boundary is essential in Lemmas 2.3.9 and 2.3.10; for the Siegel boundary this means g >= 2 (the g = 1 variant of Section 3.2.5 uses that the boundary does not meet V(f), or that the cover is finite etale).
Lemma 2.3.10 needs R0' finite normal over R0, etale outside V(I0), with no component inside V(I0).
proofSteps: Lemma 2.3.9: reduce to A0 integral; Corollary 2.3.5 gives the isomorphism with X \ Z; for g in J, H^0(U_g, O+/t)^a = A0^{1/p^infty}[g^{-1}][u^{1/p^infty}]/(uf)^a by localization; conclude from classical Hartogs on Spec A0 and injectivity of H^0(Spec A0, O/f) into H^0(Spec A0 \ V(J), O/f), using depth of O/f at least 1 on V(J).

Lemma 2.3.10(i)-(ii): the trace pairing is perfect on the complement of V(I0) and extends by normality and codimension 2; by the open mapping theorem the cokernel of R0'° -> Hom(R0'°, R0°) is killed by t^N, hence almost zero after completed perfection.

Lemma 2.3.10(iii)-(v): reduce modulo t, use the fibre-product formula for perfectoid spaces [52, Prop. 6.18]; (iv) follows from (iii); (v) uses that h in H^0(X', O+/t) cap H^0(U, O+/t) defines, via the trace pairing, a map factoring through the almost surjective trace.
Lemma 2.3.11: pass to the filtered colimit using qcqs-ness, surjectivity of X~ -> X^(i), part (v) of Lemma 2.3.10, the general Hebbarkeitssatz (Proposition 2.3.2) and base change (Lemma 2.3.4).
Corollary 2.3.12: finite extensions by Lemma 2.3.10, then the general case by Lemma 2.3.11.
acceptance: Applied in Lemma 3.2.27 to (X'*(epsilon)^perf, Z'*(epsilon)^perf, X'(epsilon)^perf) with t replaced by t^epsilon, and in Corollary 3.2.28, Proposition 3.2.34 and Theorem 3.2.36 to finite covers and inverse limits.
The t = 0 consequence (bounded functions extend) is what Corollary 3.3.17 uses to extend pi_HT across the boundary.

nodes.title: Integral (weak) canonical subgroups over p-adically complete flat Z_p^cycl-algebras
nodes.statement: Let R be a p-adically complete flat Z_p^cycl-algebra and A -> Spec R an abelian scheme with reduction A_1 over R/p. If Ha(A_1/Spec(R/p))^{(p^m - 1)/(p - 1)} divides p^epsilon for some epsilon < 1/2, there is a unique closed subgroup C_m in A[p^m], flat over R, with C_m = ker F^m modulo p^{1-epsilon}; for every p-adically complete flat Z_p^cycl-algebra R' over R, C_m(R') = {s in A[p^m](R') : s = 0 mod p^{(1-epsilon)/p^m}} (Corollary 3.2.6). C_m is called the weak canonical subgroup of level m, and a (strong) canonical subgroup if Ha(A_1/Spec(R/p))^{p^m} divides p^epsilon (Definition 3.2.7).
hypotheses: R p-adically complete and flat over Z_p^cycl; p^epsilon denotes an element of valuation epsilon, with epsilon implicitly of the form a/((p-1)p^n); the source notes Z_p^cycl could be replaced by any sufficiently ramified extension of Z_p.
0 <= epsilon < 1/2 (checked on the page image of printed pp. 974 and 978). The argument is uniform in p, including p = 2.

Theorem 3.2.1 is imported from Illusie [39, Th. VII.4.2.5(i), Rem. VII.4.2.6(i)] (obstruction theory for lifting a morphism of flat commutative group schemes along square-zero thickenings); that source is not in the library.
proofSteps: Theorem 3.2.1 (import): for flat finitely presented commutative group schemes H -> G over A and square-zero thickenings B1 -> B2 of A with ideals J_i, the obstruction to lifting (H, u) to a lift of G lies in Ext^1(H, K (x)^L J_i) with K a cone of the Lie complexes, functorially in J1 -> J2.

Corollary 3.2.2: take A = R/p, B1 = R/p^{2-epsilon}, B2 the fibre product of R/p^{2-2 epsilon} and R/p over R/p^{1-epsilon}; J1 -> J2 is multiplication by p^epsilon, so if p^epsilon is null-homotopic on the Lie complex of H = (G (x) R/p)/C1 the obstruction dies; this lifts C1 from R/p^{1-epsilon} to R/p^{2-2 epsilon}, and 2 - 2 epsilon > 1 allows iteration to R.
Remark 3.2.3 gives an alternative with worse constants using deformation theory of rings [38].
Lemma 3.2.4: if Omega^1_{X/R} is killed by p^epsilon and two sections agree modulo p^delta with delta > epsilon, they agree.
Lemma 3.2.5: Ha(A/S) is invertible iff A is ordinary (Verschiebung finite etale iff ker V has p^g geometric points).

Corollary 3.2.6 existence: H1 = ker(V^m: A_1^{(p^m)} -> A_1) has Lie complex (Lie A_1^{(p^m)} -> Lie A_1) with determinant Ha^{(p^m - 1)/(p - 1)} (m Verschiebungen); the adjugate matrix makes the determinant null-homotopic, so p^epsilon is null-homotopic; apply Corollary 3.2.2 with G = A[p^m].

Corollary 3.2.6 uniqueness: any such C_m satisfies the displayed formula, since F acts through R/p^{1-epsilon}; conversely a section vanishing modulo p^{(1-epsilon)/p^m} maps to zero in H = A[p^m]/C_m by Lemma 3.2.4 because Omega^1_{H/R} is killed by p^epsilon.
acceptance: If A has ordinary reduction (Ha invertible) every level m is allowed with epsilon = 0 and C_m is the multiplicative (connected) part of A[p^m].
The formula for C_m(R') gives the base-change compatibility used in Proposition 3.2.8(i),(ii).

nodes.title: Basic properties of strong canonical subgroups: levels, morphisms, quotients, generic fibres
nodes.statement: Let R be a p-adically complete flat Z_p^cycl-algebra and A, B -> Spec R abelian schemes. (i) If A has a canonical subgroup C_m of level m, it has one of every level m' <= m, with C_{m'} in C_m. (ii) If f: A -> B and both have canonical subgroups C_m, D_m of level m, then f maps C_m into D_m. (iii) If A has a canonical subgroup C_{m1}, then B = A/C_{m1} has a canonical subgroup D_{m2} of level m2 iff A has one of level m = m1 + m2, and then 0 -> C_{m1} -> C_m -> D_{m2} -> 0 is exact compatibly with 0 -> C_{m1} -> A -> B -> 0. (iv) If A has a canonical subgroup C_m and x is a geometric point of Spec R[1/p], then C_m(x) = (Z/p^m Z)^g with g the dimension of A at x (Proposition 3.2.8).
hypotheses: Canonical means strong canonical: Ha(A_1/Spec(R/p))^{p^m} divides p^epsilon with epsilon < 1/2.
Part (iv) uses Huber's specialization of continuous valuations [36, Prop. 2.6] to reduce to R = O_K with K algebraically closed complete of mixed characteristic.
proofSteps: (i), (ii): immediate from the displayed formula for C_m(R') in Corollary 3.2.6.

(iii): Ha(B) = Ha(A)^{p^{m1}} modulo p^{1-epsilon}; for the exact sequence check that C_m(R) maps into D_{m2}(R) modulo p^{1-epsilon}, where 0 -> ker F_A^{m1} -> ker F_A^m -> ker F_B^{m2} -> 0, and conclude by Lemma 3.2.4.

(iv): the good locus is open and closed in Spec R[1/p]; specialize a bad point to a continuous valuation of characteristic 0 [36, Prop. 2.6] and reduce to O_K; an elementary divisor count gives s in (C_m cap A[p])(K) outside C_1(K), whose image t in H = A[p]/C_1 vanishes modulo p^{(1-epsilon)/p^m}; Lemma 3.2.4 with delta = (1-epsilon)/p^m and epsilon' = epsilon/p^m < delta forces t = 0, a contradiction.
acceptance: Theorem 3.2.15(ii) uses (iv) to get a Gamma_0(p^m)-structure and (iii) for commutativity of the level-changing squares.
Test: for ordinary A over O_C, C_m is mu_{p^m}^g-like and generically (Z/p^m)^g, consistent with (iv).

nodes.title: Hartogs extension for normal rings and for the Hasse blow-up S = (R (x)^ Z_p^cycl)<u>/(fu - p^epsilon)
nodes.statement: Proposition 3.2.9: if R is normal and noetherian and Z in Spec R has codimension >= 2 everywhere, then R = H^0(Spec R \ Z, O). Lemma 3.2.10: let R be a topologically finitely generated flat p-adically complete Z_p-algebra with R/p normal, f in R whose image in R/p is not a zero divisor, 0 <= epsilon <= 1, and S = (R (x)^_{Z_p} Z_p^cycl)<u>/(fu - p^epsilon). Then S is flat and p-adically complete over Z_p^cycl, u is not a zero divisor, and for a closed Y in Spec(R/p) of codimension >= 2 with preimage Z in Spf S and complement U, H^0(U, O_{Spf S}) = H^0(Spf S, O_{Spf S}) = S.
hypotheses: Normality of the special fibre R/p and codimension >= 2 of Y; f nonzerodivisor modulo p.

In the application R is an affine open of the Siegel minimal compactification, f a lift of the Hasse invariant (not a zero divisor because the ordinary locus is dense) and Y the boundary, of codimension g; so g >= 2 is needed.
proofSteps: Proposition 3.2.9: Serre's criterion gives depth >= 2 along Z, hence vanishing of local cohomology in degrees <= 1 (SGA2 III, Exemple 3.4), hence extension (SGA2 I, Proposition 2.13).

Lemma 3.2.10 injectivity: reduce modulo p^epsilon; Spec S_epsilon is the scheme-theoretic union of {u = 0} (= Spec R_epsilon) and {f = 0} (W = V x A^1); classical Hartogs on R_epsilon and depth >= 1 of R/f along Y give injectivity of H^0(W) -> H^0(U cap W).

Surjectivity: pass to the u-adic completion S^_u, which is u-adic because u divides p^epsilon and has special fibre Spec R_epsilon, where classical Hartogs applies; then show the coefficients of u^i lie in H^0(V, O_V) (x) Z_p^cycl/p^epsilon by successive approximation.
acceptance: Remark 3.2.11: R = Z_p<T1, T2>, f = T2, epsilon = 1, Y = {T1 = T2 = 0} recovers the classical Hartogs figure.
Used in Lemma 3.2.13 (flatness), Theorem 3.2.15 (extension of Frobenius lifts and open immersions to X*) and Lemma 3.2.24.

nodes.title: The formal models X*(epsilon) of Hasse neighbourhoods and the mod-p Frobenius diagram
nodes.statement: Let X = X_{g,K^p} over Z_(p) be the Siegel moduli space, X* its minimal compactification, and X, X* their p-adic completions over Z_p^cycl. For 0 <= epsilon < 1 with p^epsilon in Z_p^cycl, X*(epsilon) -> X* is the functor on p-adically complete flat Z_p^cycl-algebras S of pairs (f, u) with f: Spf S -> X* and u in H^0(Spf S, f^* omega^{(x)(1-p)}) such that u Ha(f mod p) = p^epsilon in S/p, modulo (f, u) ~ (f, u(1 + p^{1-epsilon} h)) (Definition 3.2.12). It is represented by a formal scheme flat over Z_p^cycl, locally Spf((R (x)^ Z_p^cycl)<u>/(u Ha~ - p^epsilon)) for any local lift Ha~ of Ha; hence X*(epsilon) -> X* is an admissible blow-up (Lemma 3.2.13). Pulling back gives X(epsilon) and A(epsilon); on generic fibres X(epsilon) is the open locus |Ha| >= |p|^epsilon. Modulo p there is a natural commutative diagram (1) identifying (A(p^{-1} epsilon)/p)^{(p)}, (X(p^{-1} epsilon)/p)^{(p)} and (X*(p^{-1} epsilon)/p)^{(p)} with A(epsilon)/p, X(epsilon)/p and X*(epsilon)/p, compatibly with relative Frobenius (Lemma 3.2.14).
hypotheses: Tame level K^p in GSp_2g(A_f^p) contained in the principal congruence subgroup of level N >= 3 with p not dividing N; X parametrizes principally polarized g-dimensional abelian varieties with level-K^p structure; X* is the minimal compactification of Faltings-Chai [28] with ample omega.
The Hasse invariant Ha in H^0(X_{F_p}, omega^{(x)(p-1)}) extends to X*_{F_p}: by classical Hartogs if g >= 2 (boundary of codimension g), by direct inspection if g = 1.
Functors are restricted to flat Z_p^cycl-algebras; this is what makes the representing lift unique.
proofSteps: Lemma 3.2.13: the local right-hand side is flat by Lemma 3.2.10; given (f, u) write u Ha~ = p^epsilon (1 + p^{1-epsilon} h) and replace u by u(1 + p^{1-epsilon} h)^{-1}; uniqueness of this representative follows from flatness.

Lemma 3.2.14: relative to the diagram A/p -> X/p -> X*/p add sections u with u Ha = p^{p^{-1} epsilon} and u' with u' Ha = p^epsilon; since Ha is raised to the p-th power under division by the kernel of Frobenius, send u' to u^{(p)}.
acceptance: Generic fibre of X*(epsilon) is the locus |Ha| >= |p|^epsilon, independent of the local lift (footnote 11).
For epsilon = 0 the generic fibre is the tubular neighbourhood of the ordinary locus.

nodes.title: Canonical Frobenius lifts on Hasse neighbourhoods and the anticanonical open immersions into Gamma_0(p^m)-level
nodes.statement: Let 0 <= epsilon < 1/2. (i) There is a unique diagram of formal schemes F~: A(p^{-1} epsilon) -> A(epsilon), X(p^{-1} epsilon) -> X(epsilon), X*(p^{-1} epsilon) -> X*(epsilon) that reduces to the Frobenius diagram (1) modulo p^{1-epsilon}. (ii) For m >= 0, A(p^{-m} epsilon) has a canonical subgroup C_m of level m; the pair (A(p^{-m} epsilon)/C_m, A(p^{-m} epsilon)[p^m]/C_m) defines a morphism of generic fibres X(p^{-m} epsilon) -> X_{Gamma_0(p^m)}, which extends uniquely to X*(p^{-m} epsilon) -> X*_{Gamma_0(p^m)}; these are open immersions, and for m >= 1 the square formed with (F~_{X(p^{-m-1} epsilon)})^ad_eta and X*_{Gamma_0(p^{m+1})} -> X*_{Gamma_0(p^m)} is commutative and cartesian. (iii) A(epsilon) has a weak canonical subgroup C of level 1, and X(p^{-1} epsilon) is identified with the open and closed subset X_{Gamma_0(p)}(epsilon)_a of X_{Gamma_0(p)}(epsilon) parametrizing D in A(epsilon)[p] with D cap C = {0} (Theorem 3.2.15, Remark 3.2.16).
hypotheses: 0 <= epsilon < 1/2 (page image, printed p. 985).

Gamma_0(p^m) is Scholze's nonstandard group requiring in addition det gamma = 1 mod p^m (Definition 3.1.1), and X_{K_p} for K_p in {Gamma_0(p^m), Gamma_1(p^m), Gamma(p^m)} is the adic space of X_{K_p} (x)_{Q(zeta_{p^m})} Q_p^cycl.

The extension to the minimal compactification is proved for g >= 2 via Lemma 3.2.10; for g = 1 the source says the case is easy and left to the reader (possibly via E -> E x E into the Siegel threefold).
The statement of (iii) in the source says 'weak canonical subgroup C of level p'; the proof and later use (C in A(epsilon)[p]) show that level 1 is meant.
proofSteps: Good reduction: on X(p^{-1} epsilon) the p-th power of Ha divides p^epsilon, giving a strong canonical subgroup C of level 1; C is totally isotropic by uniqueness, so A/C is principally polarized with level-K^p structure and defines X(p^{-1} epsilon) -> X; this lifts uniquely to X(epsilon) by the Hasse invariant computation, and reduces to relative Frobenius modulo p^{1-epsilon} by definition of C.
(ii): C_m exists by Definition 3.2.7 and Corollary 3.2.6; the map to X_{Gamma_0(p^m)} uses Proposition 3.2.8(iv) and total isotropy; commutativity uses Proposition 3.2.8(iii).

Open immersion: the composite X(p^{-m} epsilon) -> X_{Gamma_0(p^m)} -> X, (A, D) -> A/D, is the forgetful open embedding, and the second map is etale; cartesianness on the good-reduction locus because both vertical maps are finite etale of degree p^{g(g+1)/2} for m >= 1.

(iii): if s in A_R[p] maps into C then s vanishes in A'_R[p] modulo p^{(1-epsilon)/p}, so its image t in H = A_R[p]/C_0 vanishes modulo p^{(1-epsilon)/p}; since Ha kills Omega^1_H and divides p^{epsilon/p}, Lemma 3.2.4 with delta = (1-epsilon)/p, epsilon' = epsilon/p gives t = 0.

Extension to X* for g >= 2: Lemma 3.2.10 with f = Ha extends F~; open immersions into finite normal Y extend because a finite, generically open section into a normal space is open and closed; cartesianness again by Hartogs.
acceptance: On the ordinary locus (epsilon = 0) the tower X_{Gamma_0(p^m)}(0)_a is the anticanonical locus D[p] cap C = {0} (Section 3.1 toy example for Gamma_0(p) on the modular curve).
The finite locally free Frobenius lift F~ realizes the transition maps of the anticanonical tower as relative Frobenius modulo p^{1-epsilon}.

nodes.title: The anticanonical Gamma_0(p^m)-tower on the minimal compactification and its affinoidness at deep level
nodes.statement: For m >= 1 define X_{Gamma_0(p^m)}(epsilon)_a in X_{Gamma_0(p^m)} and X*_{Gamma_0(p^m)}(epsilon)_a in X*_{Gamma_0(p^m)} as the images of X(p^{-m} epsilon) and X*(p^{-m} epsilon). X*_{Gamma_0(p^m)}(epsilon)_a is open and closed in X*_{Gamma_0(p^m)}(epsilon) (open by Theorem 3.2.15, closed because X*(p^{-m} epsilon) -> X*(epsilon) is finite) and is the locus where the universal totally isotropic D in A(epsilon)[p^m] has D[p] cap C = {0}. The resulting tower ... -> X*_{Gamma_0(p^{m+1})}(epsilon)_a -> X*_{Gamma_0(p^m)}(epsilon)_a -> ... is the pullback of the full Gamma_0-tower along the open X*_{Gamma_0(p)}(epsilon)_a, it has integral models X*(p^{-m} epsilon) whose transition maps are relative Frobenius modulo p^{1-epsilon}, and carries the abelian schemes A_{Gamma_0(p^m)}(epsilon)_a by pullback. Lemma 3.2.17: for fixed 0 <= epsilon < 1/2 and m sufficiently large, X*_{Gamma_0(p^m)}(epsilon)_a is affinoid.
hypotheses: 0 <= epsilon < 1/2; notation X_{K_p}(epsilon) for preimages of X(epsilon).
Lemma 3.2.17 uses Serre vanishing H^i(X*, omega^{(x) p^m (p-1)}) = 0 for i > 0 on the projective integral minimal compactification with ample omega.
proofSteps: Openness and closedness as stated, using Theorem 3.2.15 and finiteness of X*(p^{-m} epsilon) -> X*(epsilon).

Lemma 3.2.17: choose m with H^i(X*, omega^{(x) p^m (p-1)}) = 0 for i > 0, lift Ha^{p^m} globally; |Ha| >= |p|^{p^{-m} epsilon} iff |Ha~^{p^m}| >= |p|^epsilon, a non-vanishing condition for a section of an ample line bundle, which defines an affinoid space X*(p^{-m} epsilon) = X*_{Gamma_0(p^m)}(epsilon)_a.
acceptance: Check that the level-m piece is the pullback of the level-(m+1) piece along the cartesian square of Theorem 3.2.15(ii).
Affinoidness at deep level is what makes Lemma 3.2.24 and Proposition 3.2.33 statements about global sections.

nodes.title: The anticanonical Gamma_0(p^infty)-tower is perfectoid and tilts to the perfected Hasse locus in characteristic p
nodes.statement: Let 0 <= epsilon < 1/2. There are unique perfectoid spaces X_{Gamma_0(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a, X*_{Gamma_0(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a and A_{Gamma_0(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a over Q_p^cycl with X_{Gamma_0(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a ~ lim_m X_{Gamma_0(p^m)}(epsilon)_a and similarly for the other two, where ~ is in the sense of [55, Def. 2.4.1]. The tilt of X*_{Gamma_0(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a is the open subset X'*perf(epsilon) of X'*perf where |Ha| >= |t|^epsilon, and the tilt of A_{Gamma_0(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a is the corresponding open A'perf(epsilon) (Corollary 3.2.19). Here t in (Z_p^cycl)^flat has |t| = |t^sharp| = |p| and a (p-1)-th root, (Z_p^cycl)^flat = F_p[[t^{1/(p-1)p^infty}]], X' is the t-adic completion of X_{g,K^p} (x) F_p[[t^{1/(p-1)p^infty}]], and perfections are inverse limits along relative Frobenius (Definition 3.2.18).
hypotheses: 0 <= epsilon < 1/2.

The relation ~ is the Scholze-Weinstein notion: homeomorphism on underlying spaces plus dense image of colimits of affinoid sections on an affinoid cover; it is stronger than the residue-field notion of Perfectoid Spaces Definition 7.14 ([55], remark after Theorem 2.4.7).

Inputs from [52]: Definition 5.1(ii) and Lemma 5.6 (perfectoid K°a-algebras and perfectoid K-algebras) and Theorem 5.2 (tilting equivalence); from [55]: Proposition 2.4.2 (~ for completed direct limits) and Proposition 2.4.5 (uniqueness).
proofSteps: Define X_{Gamma_0(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a = lim_m X(p^{-m} epsilon) as formal schemes over Z_p^cycl; locally R_infty is the p-adic completion of colim R_m, flat over Z_p^cycl.

Since the transitions R_m/p^{1-epsilon} -> R_{m+1}/p^{1-epsilon} are relative Frobenius, absolute Frobenius gives R_infty/p^{(1-epsilon)/p} = R_infty/p^{1-epsilon}; by [52, Def. 5.1(ii)] R_infty^a is a perfectoid Z_p^cycl a-algebra and R_infty[1/p] is perfectoid [52, Lemma 5.6].
The generic fibre is perfectoid with ~ lim by [55, Def. 2.4.1, Prop. 2.4.2], unique by [55, Prop. 2.4.5].

Tilt: the characteristic-p analogue X'*(epsilon) (u Ha = t^epsilon) has relative Frobenius transition maps and perfection X'*(epsilon)^perf with generic fibre the locus |Ha| >= |t|^epsilon in X'*perf.

By Theorem 3.2.15(i), X'*(p^{-m} epsilon)/t^{1-epsilon} = X*(p^{-m} epsilon)/p^{1-epsilon} compatibly with transitions, so R_infty/p^{1-epsilon} = S_infty/t^{1-epsilon}, and [52, Th. 5.2] identifies R_infty[1/p] and S_infty[1/t] as tilts.
acceptance: For g = 1 and epsilon = 0: the anticanonical ordinary Gamma_0(p^infty)-tower tilts to the perfection of the ordinary locus of the modular curve in characteristic p.
Check that the affine formal opens Spf R_infty and Spf S_infty correspond under the identification modulo p^{1-epsilon} = t^{1-epsilon}.

In characteristic p, X'*(epsilon) = {|Ha| >= |t|^epsilon} in X'* is affinoid and the boundary Z'(epsilon) is Zariski closed; perfection yields an affinoid perfectoid space with a Zariski closed embedding, which is strongly Zariski closed by Lemma 2.2.5.

nodes.title: Tate's normalized traces from Gamma_0(p^infty)-level to finite level on the good-reduction anticanonical tower
nodes.statement: Lemma 3.2.21: let R be p-adically complete flat over Z_p, Y_1, ..., Y_n in R and P_1, ..., P_n in R<X_1, ..., X_n> topologically nilpotent, S = R<X>/(X_i^p - Y_i - P_i); then S is finite free over R with basis the monomials X^i (0 <= i_j <= p-1), and tr_{S/R}(S) is contained in I^n with I = (p, I_1, ..., I_n), I_i the ideal of coefficients of P_i. Corollary 3.2.22: let R be p-adically complete, topologically of finite type and formally smooth of dimension n over Z_p, f in R nonzerodivisor modulo p, R_epsilon = (R (x)^ Z_p^cycl)<u_epsilon>/(f u_epsilon - p^epsilon) for 0 <= epsilon < 1, and phi: R_epsilon -> R_{epsilon/p} a Z_p^cycl-algebra map that is Frobenius on R/p and u_epsilon -> u_{epsilon/p}^p modulo p^{1-epsilon}; if epsilon < 1/2 then phi[1/p] is finite flat and the trace maps R_{epsilon/p} into p^{n-(2n+1) epsilon} R_epsilon. Corollary 3.2.23: for 0 <= epsilon < 1/2 and m' >= m, the maps p^{-(m'-m) g(g+1)/2} tr: O_{X(p^{-m'} epsilon)}[1/p] -> O_{X(p^{-m} epsilon)}[1/p] are compatible, the image of colim_{m'} O_{X(p^{-m'} epsilon)} lies in p^{-C_m} O_{X(p^{-m} epsilon)} with C_m -> 0, and they extend to continuous normalized traces tr_m: O_{X_{Gamma_0(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a}[1/p] -> O_{X(p^{-m} epsilon)}[1/p] with x = lim_m tr_m(x).
hypotheses: Formal smoothness is available only on the good-reduction locus X(p^{-m} epsilon) (open Siegel moduli), of relative dimension n = g(g+1)/2.
0 <= epsilon < 1/2 is needed so that epsilon < 1 - epsilon in the factorization argument of Corollary 3.2.22.

Constants are as printed: Corollary 3.2.22(ii) states p^{n-(2n+1) epsilon}; its proof shows the auxiliary trace lands in p^{n-2n epsilon}; Corollary 3.2.23 uses p^{-(g^2+g+1) epsilon/p^m} (page images, printed pp. 993-995).
proofSteps: Lemma 3.2.21(i): modulo I the presentation is a regular embedding; Koszul complexes C_k over R/I^k are perfect and acyclic off degree 0, giving freeness modulo I^k and in the limit.

Lemma 3.2.21(ii): reduce to Y_i = 1 (faithfully flat base change), then Y_i = 0 after translation, to tr(X_1) in I^n, to the universal coefficient ring Z_p[[a]], and prove tr(X_1) lies in each ideal p^k I_1 + I_{j1} + ... + I_{jk}, whose intersection is contained in I^n.

Corollary 3.2.22: locally Spf R is etale over Spf Z_p<Y_1..Y_n>, so R is free over itself via Frobenius; compare with R'_{epsilon/p} = (R (x)^ Z_p^cycl)<v>/(f^p v - p^epsilon) via tau: v -> u^p, whose cokernel is killed by p^epsilon; factor phi through psi: R_epsilon -> R'_{epsilon/p} and write R'_{epsilon/p} = R_epsilon<X>/(X_i^p - Y_i - P_i) with P_i in p^{1-2 epsilon} R_epsilon<X>; apply Lemma 3.2.21.

Corollary 3.2.23: by Theorem 3.2.15(i) the transition maps F~ are of the type of Corollary 3.2.22 with epsilon' = p^{-m} epsilon and n = g(g+1)/2, so the normalized trace loses p^{-(g^2+g+1) epsilon/p^m}; the sum over m' >= m converges, giving C_m -> 0, continuity and the limit formula.
acceptance: Test on the ordinary torus-type model R = Z_p<Y^{+-1}>, f = 1: the normalized trace from Z_p^cycl<Y^{1/p^infty}> to level m is the classical Tate normalized trace.
Used in Lemma 3.2.24(ii) to produce retractions and density.

nodes.title: Hartogs extension at Gamma_0(p^infty)-level for finite normal covers etale away from the boundary
nodes.statement: Assume g >= 2 and 0 <= epsilon < 1/2. Let Y*_m -> X*_{Gamma_0(p^m)}(epsilon)_a be finite, etale away from the boundary, with Y*_m normal and no irreducible component mapping into the boundary; let Y_m be the preimage of the good-reduction part, Y*_{m'} (m' >= m) the normalization of the pullback, and Y_infty the pullback of Y_m to X_{Gamma_0(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a. Write Y*_{m'} = Spa(S_{m'}, S_{m'}^+) for m' large (affinoid by Lemma 3.2.17). Then (i) S_{m'}^+ = H^0(Y_{m'}, O^+) for m' large; (ii) colim_{m'} S_{m'}^+ -> H^0(Y_infty, O^+) is injective with dense image and there are continuous retractions H^0(Y_infty, O) -> S_{m'}; (iii) if S_infty = H^0(Y_infty, O) is a perfectoid Q_p^cycl-algebra, then Y*_infty = Spa(S_infty, S_infty^+) is affinoid perfectoid, Y*_infty ~ lim Y*_{m'}, and S_infty^+ is the p-adic completion of colim S_{m'}^+ (Lemma 3.2.24).
hypotheses: g >= 2 (boundary codimension >= 2); the g = 1 variant is handled separately after Proposition 3.2.33.
Y*_m finite normal, etale away from the boundary, no component in the boundary.
proofSteps: (i): with R = H^0(X*_{Gamma_0(p^m)}(epsilon)_a, O) and S = S_m, both normal noetherian with boundary of codimension >= 2; the trace S -> R exists away from the boundary and extends; the trace pairing induces S = Hom_R(S, R) by extension across codimension 2.

As in Lemma 2.3.10(iii), H^0(V, O_{Y*}) = Hom_R(S, H^0(U, O)) for opens U with preimage V, so (i) reduces to H^0(X_{Gamma_0(p^m)}(epsilon)_a, O^+) = H^0(X*_{Gamma_0(p^m)}(epsilon)_a, O^+), which is Lemma 3.2.10.
(ii): Tate's normalized traces (Corollary 3.2.23) with (i) give retractions and injectivity; convergence tr_m(x) -> x gives density.
(iii): immediate from (ii).
acceptance: Applied with Y*_m = X*_{Gamma_1(p^m)}(epsilon)_a in Lemmas 3.2.29-3.2.32.
Check (i) on the trivial cover Y*_m = X*_{Gamma_0(p^m)}(epsilon)_a, where it is Lemma 3.2.10.

nodes.title: Adding Gamma_1(p^m)-structure: guess the tilt as a perfected normalization and prove it is the untilt
nodes.statement: Assume g >= 2 and 0 <= epsilon < 1/2. Let D_m = A_{Gamma_0(p^m)}(epsilon)_a[p^m]/C_m on the anticanonical tower; then A_{Gamma_0(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a[p^m] -> D_{m,Gamma_0(p^infty)} is an isomorphism of perfectoid spaces (Lemma 3.2.25) and its tilt is the perfection of D'_m = A'(epsilon)[p^m]/C'_m (Lemma 3.2.26). In characteristic p let X^{ord*}_{Gamma_1(p^m)} = Spec H^0(X^ord_{Gamma_1(p^m)}, O), finite over the affine ordinary minimal locus X^{ord*}, and X'*_{Gamma_1(p^m)}(epsilon) its Hasse-locus generic fibre; the triple (X'*(epsilon)^perf, Z'*(epsilon)^perf, X'(epsilon)^perf) is good (Lemma 3.2.27) and so is its Gamma_1(p^m) analogue (Corollary 3.2.28). For Y*_m = X*_{Gamma_1(p^m)}(epsilon)_a, the tilt of Y_infty is X'_{Gamma_1(p^m)}(epsilon)^perf (Lemma 3.2.29), the tilt of Y*_infty \ boundary is X'*_{Gamma_1(p^m)}(epsilon)^perf \ boundary (Lemma 3.2.30, via Lemma 3.2.31), and S_infty = H^0(Y_infty, O) is perfectoid with tilt X'*_{Gamma_1(p^m)}(epsilon)^perf (Lemma 3.2.32). Consequently (Proposition 3.2.33) for m >= 1 there is a unique perfectoid X*_{Gamma_1(p^m) cap Gamma_0(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a ~ lim_{m'} X*_{Gamma_1(p^m) cap Gamma_0(p^{m'})}(epsilon)_a, affinoid together with the finite levels for m' large, with dense image of global sections and a good triple with its boundary and good-reduction locus; and (Proposition 3.2.34) the same holds for X*_{Gamma_1(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a ~ lim_m X*_{Gamma_1(p^m)}(epsilon)_a.
hypotheses: g >= 2 for Lemmas 3.2.24, 3.2.27, 3.2.28 and the construction of X^{ord*}_{Gamma_1(p^m)}; for g = 1 the source notes that X*_{Gamma_1(p^m)}(epsilon)_a -> X*_{Gamma_0(p^m)}(epsilon)_a is finite etale, the boundary lies in the ordinary locus, and Lemmas 2.3.9-2.3.10 still apply in codimension 1 under those conditions.
Lemma 3.2.27 needs a resolution of singularities of X* (x) F_p, supplied by the toroidal compactification of Faltings-Chai [28].
Lemma 3.2.31: for finite etale Y1, Y2 -> X over a perfectoid field and U in X with H^0(X, O) injecting into H^0(U, O), a map f: Y1 -> Y2 over X that is an isomorphism over U is an isomorphism.
proofSteps: Lemma 3.2.25: the transition A_{Gamma_0(p^{m'+m})}[p^m] -> A_{Gamma_0(p^{m'})}[p^m] kills C_m and so factors through D_m; compare the inverse limits on perfectoid test algebras.
Lemma 3.2.26: perfection kills ker Frobenius = C'_m, so (D'_m)^perf = A'(epsilon)[p^m]^perf, the tilt of A_{Gamma_0(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a[p^m] by Corollary 3.2.19.
Lemma 3.2.27: locally over affine opens of X'*, apply Lemma 2.3.9 with t replaced by t^epsilon (and Corollary 2.3.12); Corollary 3.2.28 follows by Lemma 2.3.10.
Lemma 3.2.29: Y_infty -> X_{Gamma_0(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a parametrizes isomorphisms D_{m,Gamma_0(p^infty)} = (Z/p^m)^g, whose tilt parametrizes (D'_m)^perf = (Z/p^m)^g by Lemma 3.2.26.

Lemma 3.2.30: untilt X'*_{Gamma_1(p^m)}(epsilon)^perf = Spa(T, T+) to (U, U+); get U+ -> S_infty^+ and maps of adic spaces away from the boundary; both sides are perfectoid finite etale over X*_{Gamma_0(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a \ boundary; conclude with Lemmas 3.2.27 and 3.2.31.

Lemma 3.2.32: U+/p injects into S_infty^+/p almost (goodness, Corollary 3.2.28), and S_infty^+/p injects into H^0(Y*_infty \ boundary, O+/p) = (U+/p)^a (Lemma 3.2.30, Corollary 3.2.28), so U = S_infty.
Propositions 3.2.33-3.2.34: combine with Lemma 3.2.24(iii); pass to the limit over m using Lemma 2.3.11.
acceptance: Check on the ordinary locus epsilon = 0 that the characteristic-p candidate is the perfected normalization of the Igusa-type cover trivializing D'_m.
The resulting triple (X*_{Gamma_1(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a, boundary, good-reduction part) is good, which is what later extends pi_HT.

nodes.statement: Lemma 3.2.35: for m >= 1, X*_{Gamma(p^m)}(epsilon)_a -> X*_{Gamma_1(p^m)}(epsilon)_a is finite etale. Theorem 3.2.36: there is a unique perfectoid space X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a over Q_p^cycl with X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a ~ lim_m X*_{Gamma(p^m)}(epsilon)_a; it and X*_{Gamma(p^m)}(epsilon)_a for m large are affinoid, colim_m H^0(X*_{Gamma(p^m)}(epsilon)_a, O) -> H^0(X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a, O) has dense image, and with Z_{Gamma(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a the boundary and X_{Gamma(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a the preimage of X_{Gamma_0(p)}(epsilon)_a, the triple (X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a, Z_{Gamma(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a, X_{Gamma(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a) is good.
hypotheses: 0 <= epsilon < 1/2 as in Section 3.2.
Lemma 3.2.35 is proved for g >= 2; the case g = 1 is left to the reader.

The step from epsilon = 0 to general epsilon uses a description of the boundary strata of X*_{Gamma(p^m)} -> X*_{Gamma_1(p^m)} in terms of lower-dimensional Siegel moduli spaces, asserted but not proved in the source.
proofSteps: Lemma 3.2.35, epsilon = 0: by Hartogs (Lemma 3.2.24) it suffices to decompose the good ordinary part X_{Gamma(p^m)}(0)_a as a disjoint union over Gamma_1(p^m)/Gamma(p^m) of copies of X_{Gamma_1(p^m)}(0)_a: a symplectic alpha: A[p^m] = (Z/p^m)^{2g} is equivalent to (D_m, alpha_0, Sigma) with Sigma = alpha(C_m) a totally isotropic complement of (Z/p^m)^g (+) 0^g, on which Gamma_1(p^m)/Gamma(p^m) acts simply transitively.

General epsilon: above any locally closed boundary stratum meeting X*_{Gamma_1(p^m)}(0)_a the map is finite etale since it is so generically; every stratum meeting the epsilon-locus meets the ordinary locus.

Theorem 3.2.36: almost purity [52, Th. 7.9(iii)] makes the finite etale pullbacks perfectoid at Gamma_1(p^infty) cap Gamma(p^m) level; Lemmas 2.3.10 and 2.3.11 carry goodness to the finite covers and the inverse limit.
acceptance: Summary statement in the source: a strict and explicit neighbourhood of the ordinary locus in the minimal compactification becomes affinoid perfectoid in the limit and satisfies the Hebbarkeitssatz with respect to the boundary.
The triple's goodness with t = 0 yields the extension of bounded functions used in Corollary 3.3.17 and Theorem 3.3.18(vi).

nodes.title: Hodge-Tate filtration and Hasse invariant of an abelian variety with bad reduction via its connected Neron model
nodes.statement: Proposition 3.3.1: let C be algebraically closed complete over Q_p and A/C an abelian variety with connected Neron model G/O_C; its p-adic completion is an extension 0 -> T^ -> G^ -> B^ -> 0 of an abelian scheme B over O_C by a split torus T, G^[p^infty] is a p-divisible group over O_C, and the Hodge-Tate filtration Lie G^ (x) C(1) -> T_p G^ (x) C is compatible with the Hodge-Tate filtration Lie A(1) -> T_p A (x) C of A. Lemma 3.3.2: if A comes from x in X(C) = X_{g,K^p}(C), extended to x in X*_{g,K^p}(O_C) by properness, then (i) x^* omega_{X*} = omega_G, and (ii) modulo p, Ha(x) = Ha(B (x) O_C/p) (x) (omega_T^can)^{p-1} in omega_G^{(x)(p-1)}/p = omega_B^{(x)(p-1)}/p (x) omega_T^{(x)(p-1)}/p, where omega_T^can = dlog Z_1 ^ ... ^ dlog Z_m up to sign.
hypotheses: C algebraically closed and complete; A has connected Neron model (semistable reduction after the implicit base change over C).
The sign ambiguity of omega_T^can disappears in the (p-1)-th power for p != 2, and modulo p for p = 2 (footnote 14).
Proposition 3.3.1's proof is 'identical to the proof of [54, Prop. 4.15]' (Scholze, Perfectoid spaces: a survey), which is not in the library.
Lemma 3.3.2 uses a smooth projective toroidal compactification of Faltings-Chai [28] with its semiabelian family G^univ and omega_{G^univ} = f^* omega_{X*}.
proofSteps: Proposition 3.3.1: by reference to [54, Prop. 4.15] (unread import).
Lemma 3.3.2(i): pull back omega_{G^univ} = f^* omega_{X*} from the toroidal compactification to x.

Lemma 3.3.2(ii): the Verschiebung of G^univ in characteristic p defines Ha' in H^0(Xbar (x) F_p, omega_{G^univ}^{(x)(p-1)}) extending Ha, hence equal to the pullback of Ha; pulling back to x reduces to a direct verification on the torus and abelian parts.
acceptance: For a Tate curve over C: B = 0, G^ = G_m^, Ha(x) is the canonical differential to the (p-1)-th power, so the point lies in the ordinary locus, and the Hodge-Tate filtration is Q_p-rational.
Used for K-rationality of the filtration in Lemma 3.3.4 and for the induction on g in Lemmas 3.3.8 and 3.3.15.

nodes.title: The GSp_2g(Q_p)-equivariant continuous Hodge-Tate map on the open infinite-level Siegel tower
nodes.statement: Set |X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}| = lim_m |X*_{Gamma(p^m)}|, |Z_{Gamma(p^infty)}| = lim |Z_{Gamma(p^m)}| and |X_{Gamma(p^infty)}| = lim |X_{Gamma(p^m)}| with their continuous GSp_2g(Q_p)-actions; for a complete nonarchimedean K over Q_p^cycl with open bounded valuation subring K+, X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}(K, K+) = lim_m X*_{Gamma(p^m)}(K, K+), and |X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}| is the (non-filtered) colimit of these sets, each point coming from a unique minimal (K, K+) (Remark 3.3.3). There is a GSp_2g(Q_p)-equivariant continuous map |pi_HT|: |X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}| \ |Z_{Gamma(p^infty)}| -> |Fl| sending a point given by a principally polarized abelian variety A/K with symplectic alpha: T_p A = Z_p^{2g} to the Hodge-Tate filtration Lie A in K^{2g} (Lemma 3.3.4).
hypotheses: Fl is the adic flag variety over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) of totally isotropic g-dimensional subspaces of the split symplectic space of dimension 2g; working over Q_p^cycl, Tate twists are ignored.

The comparison input is [53, Th. 1.3] (primitive comparison for proper smooth morphisms of smooth adic spaces), applied to the universal abelian variety over S = X* \ Z; [54, Prop. 4.10] identifies the resulting map with the Hodge-Tate filtration at geometric points; [30, Ch. 2, App. C] gives K-rationality for p-divisible groups.
Local pro-finite etale affinoid perfectoid covers of the smooth space S exist ([53], supplied by the pro-etale theory).
proofSteps: K-rationality: by Proposition 3.3.1 the filtration, a priori over the completed algebraic closure of K, is K-rational since this holds for p-divisible groups [30, Ch. 2, App. C]; this defines the map on points.

Continuity: for g: A_S -> S proper smooth, [53, Th. 1.3] gives almost isomorphisms (R^1 g_* Z/p^n) (x) O_S^+/p^n -> R^1 g_* O^+_{A_S}/p^n; passing to S_proet, the limit over n and inverting p gives R^1 g_* Z^_p (x) O^_S = R^1 g_* O^_{A_S}, hence a map (R^1 g_* O_{A_S}) (x) O^_S -> R^1 g_* Q^_p (x) O^_S with R^1 g_* O_{A_S} = Lie A_S via the principal polarization.

On an affinoid perfectoid pro-finite etale U~ -> U in S, the pullback U~_infty = U~ x_S (X*_{Gamma(p^infty)} \ Z) is affinoid perfectoid and the tautological trivialization gives Lie A_S (x) O_{U~_infty} -> O^{2g}_{U~_infty}, totally isotropic, defining U~_infty -> Fl that agrees on geometric points with the Hodge-Tate filtration [54, Prop. 4.10].
Since |U~_infty| -> |U| x_{|S|} (|X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}| \ |Z|) is the realization of a pro-etale surjection and pro-etale maps are open, continuity descends.
acceptance: Equivariance is clear from the moduli description; the map depends only on the p-divisible group with trivialized Tate module.
For g = 1 on the supersingular locus, |pi_HT| lands in Drinfeld's upper half plane, and on the ordinary locus it records the position of the canonical subgroup (Section 3.1 discussion).

nodes.title: The closure of the ordinary locus is the preimage of the Q_p-rational flags
nodes.statement: Definition 3.3.5: a subset U of |X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}| is affinoid perfectoid if it is the preimage of an affinoid U_m = Spa(R_m, R_m^+) of X*_{Gamma(p^m)} for all large m and (R_infty, R_infty^+) is an affinoid perfectoid Q_p^cycl-algebra, with R_infty^+ the p-adic completion of colim R_m^+; it is perfectoid if covered by affinoid perfectoid subsets, and perfectoid subsets carry a glued perfectoid space structure; X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a is affinoid perfectoid by Theorem 3.2.36 and the notion is GSp_2g(Q_p)-stable. Lemma 3.3.6: the preimage of Fl(Q_p) under |pi_HT| is the closure of |X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}(0)| \ |Z_{Gamma(p^infty)}(0)| (a retro-compact open, so the closure is its set of specializations).
hypotheses: X*(epsilon) is the locus |Ha| >= |p|^epsilon for epsilon < 1, independent of the lift; epsilon = 0 is the tubular neighbourhood of the ordinary locus in the special fibre.

The converse direction uses either the classification of p-divisible groups over O_C [55, Th. B] or the direct argument of Remark 3.3.7: for a p-divisible group G over O_C the kernel of alpha_G: T_p G -> Lie G^* is T_p(G^mult).
proofSteps: Reduce to rank-one points x = x~ with values in (C, O_C): specialization preserves both conditions by continuity and retro-compactness.
By Lemma 3.3.2 the Hasse invariant at x is invertible iff the abelian part B of the Neron model is ordinary; by Proposition 3.3.1, pi_HT(x) in Fl(Q_p) iff Lie B (x) C in T_p B (x) C is Q_p-rational.
If B is ordinary, B[p^infty] = (Q_p/Z_p)^g x mu_{p^infty}^g and the filtration is rational (measuring the canonical subgroup).

Conversely, rational filtration means ker alpha_G is g-dimensional, so by Remark 3.3.7 the multiplicative part has dimension g and B is ordinary (alternatively by [55, Th. B], since rational totally isotropic subspaces form one GSp_2g(Z_p)-orbit).
acceptance: g = 1: the ordinary locus maps to P^1(Q_p) and the supersingular locus to Omega^2 = P^1 \ P^1(Q_p).
Remark 3.3.7 test: for G = mu_{p^infty} the kernel of alpha_G is all of T_p G; for G etale it is zero.

(|X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}(epsilon)| \ |Z_{Gamma(p^infty)}(epsilon)|). Lemma 3.3.11: with the same gamma_i, |X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}| = union of gamma_i . |X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}(epsilon)|.
hypotheses: 0 < epsilon < 1 (page image, printed p. 1009).

Plucker charts: for J in {1, ..., 2g} of cardinality g, Fl_J is the affinoid where |s_J'| <= |s_J| for all J'; GSp_2g(Z_p) permutes them transitively; Fl_{g+1..2g}(Q_p) consists of totally isotropic direct summands M of Z_p^{2g} with M (+) (Z_p^g (+) 0^g) = Z_p^{2g}.

Lemma 3.3.9: replace U by its GSp_2g(Q_p)-saturation; it contains Fl(Q_p); the diagonal element gamma = (1, ..., 1, p, ..., p) contracts Fl_{1..g} to the point Q_p^g (+) 0^g, so by quasi-compactness gamma^n(Fl_{1..g}) lies in U for some n, and Fl_{1..g} is in U.
Lemma 3.3.10: cover the quasi-compact Fl by finitely many gamma_i . U and pull back along |pi_HT|.

Lemma 3.3.11: the union V is quasi-compact open containing the open part, hence the preimage of some V_m at finite level containing X*_{Gamma(p^m)} \ Z_{Gamma(p^m)}; a classical point outside V_m would have an open neighbourhood inside the boundary, impossible for dimension reasons.

nodes.title: The minimally compactified Siegel tower at Gamma(p^infty)-level is perfectoid, covered by finitely many translates
nodes.statement: There exists a perfectoid space X*_{Gamma(p^infty)} over Q_p^cycl with X*_{Gamma(p^infty)} ~ lim_m X*_{Gamma(p^m)}; it is covered by finitely many GSp_2g(Q_p)-translates of the affinoid perfectoid X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a, for any 0 < epsilon < 1/2 (Corollary 3.3.12). Its boundary Z_{Gamma(p^infty)} carries an induced perfectoid structure. Theorem 3.1.2(i) records the resulting statement with uniqueness up to unique isomorphism and a GSp_2g(Q_p)-action equivariant for the tilde-limit.
hypotheses: Tame level K^p contained in the principal congruence subgroup of level N >= 3 prime to p (Theorem 3.1.2); 0 < epsilon < 1/2.
The GSp_2g(Q_p)-action does not preserve the structure map to Spa(Q_p^cycl, Z_p^cycl) (footnote 7).

X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}(epsilon) = GSp_2g(Z_p) . X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a, and the latter is affinoid perfectoid by Theorem 3.2.36; affinoid perfectoidness is GSp_2g(Q_p)-stable.
Glue the Spa(R_infty, R_infty^+) on the affinoid perfectoid subsets (Definition 3.3.5); ~ lim holds because it holds on each piece.

nodes.title: The Hodge-Tate period map as a map of adic spaces and its extension over the boundary
nodes.statement: Corollary 3.3.13: there is a unique map of adic spaces pi_HT: X*_{Gamma(p^infty)} \ Z_{Gamma(p^infty)} -> Fl realizing |pi_HT|. Lemma 3.3.14: the preimage of Fl_{g+1..2g}(Q_p) is the closure of X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}(0)_a \ Z_{Gamma(p^infty)}(0)_a. Lemma 3.3.15: for any open U in Fl containing Fl(Q_p) there is epsilon > 0 with X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}(epsilon) \ Z(epsilon) in pi_HT^{-1}(U). Lemma 3.3.16: there is 0 < epsilon < 1/2 with X*_{Gamma(p^infty)}(epsilon)_a \ Z(epsilon)_a in pi_HT^{-1}(Fl_{g+1..2g}). Corollary 3.3.17: pi_HT extends uniquely to a map of adic spaces pi_HT: X*_{Gamma(p^infty)} -> Fl.
hypotheses: Fl_{g+1..2g} is an open affinoid Plucker chart; the anticanonical condition matches C (+) D = T_p A with D = alpha^{-1}(Z_p^g (+) 0^g).
The boundary extension relies on the goodness (Hebbarkeitssatz with t = 0) of the triple in Theorem 3.2.36.
proofSteps: Corollary 3.3.13: uniqueness is clear; existence as in Lemma 3.3.4 using affinoid perfectoid subsets of X*_{Gamma(p^infty)} \ Z in place of U~_infty.

nodes.title: Hodge-type setup: fixed symplectic embedding, finite maps to Siegel varieties, and the image compactification
nodes.statement: Scholze Section 4.1: (G, D) is of Hodge type if it admits a closed embedding (G, D) -> (G', D') = (Sp_2g, D_{Sp_2g}); one such embedding is fixed and all later constructions depend on it a priori. With X_K, X*_K (K in G(A_f)) and Y_{K'}, Y*_{K'} (K' in G'(A_f)) the locally symmetric varieties over C, there are natural finite maps X_K -> Y_{K'} and X*_K -> Y*_{K'} whenever K = K' cap G(A_f); by [25, Prop. 1.15] for every K there is such a K' making X_K -> Y_{K'} a closed embedding, while the analogous statement for minimal compactifications is not known. The image compactification (written with an overbar in the source) is defined by the universal finite map X*_K -> Xbar*_K over which all X*_K -> Y*_{K'} with K = K' cap G(A_f) factor; it is the scheme-theoretic image of X*_K in Y*_{K'} for K' small enough, and G(A_f) still acts on the tower. omega_K on Xbar*_K is pulled back from the ample omega_{K'} on Y*_{K'}, and Fl denotes the Siegel flag variety of totally isotropic subspaces of C^{2g}. Caraiani-Scholze Section 2.1 and Hansen-Johansson Section 5.2 use the Deligne-style variant: a closed embedding of Shimura data (G, X) -> (GSp_2g, H_g^{+-}), and by [Del71, Prop. 1.15] a closed embedding S_K -> S~_{K~} (x)_Q E for suitable K~ with K = K~ cap G(A_f).
hypotheses: Chapter 4 conventions of Scholze (stated 'for convenience'): G^der simply connected, D a G(R)-conjugacy class of u: U(1) -> G^ad_R with ad u(-1) a Cartan involution and mu minuscule; hence G has a compact inner form and G(R) is connected; everything is base changed to C via a fixed isomorphism C = Qbar_p (fields of definition ignored).
Footnote 15: allowing general symplectic Q-vector spaces gives an equivalent notion by Zarhin's trick.

The image compactification Xbar*_K need not be normal and need not equal the minimal compactification X*_K; Hansen-Johansson and Boxer-Pilloni stress that the genuine minimal compactification only maps to it.

Closed embedding at open level: [25, Prop. 1.15] (Deligne, Travaux de Shimura) cited, not read.
Existence of the universal finite map: everything is of finite type, so the scheme-theoretic image of X*_K in Y*_{K'} stabilizes for K' small enough.
acceptance: For G = Sp_2g with the identity embedding, Xbar*_K = X*_K.

nodes.statement: Hansen-Johansson Definition 5.4: a map of perfectoid spaces Z -> X is a Zariski-closed embedding if Z x_X U -> U is a Zariski-closed embedding of affinoid perfectoid spaces in the sense of [Sch15, Section 2.2] for every open affinoid perfectoid U in X; a perfectoid space X over Spa(K, K+) is analytically separated if its diagonal is a Zariski-closed embedding. Lemma 5.5(2): in an analytically separated perfectoid space, the intersection of two open affinoid perfectoid subsets is affinoid perfectoid. Lemma 5.6: if (X_i) is a cofiltered inverse system of separated rigid analytic spaces over Spa(K, K°), each open in the analytification of a projective variety, and X_infty = lim X_i^diamond is a perfectoid space, then X_infty is analytically separated. Lemma 5.7: for a closed immersion Y -> X of quasi-projective varieties over a nonarchimedean field K and a perfectoid space Z with a map to X^an, the diamond W = Z x_{X^an} Y^an is a perfectoid space and W -> Z is a Zariski-closed embedding.
hypotheses: The source cautions that it is not clear whether being a Zariski-closed embedding can be checked on a single affinoid cover or is stable under base change.

Lemma 5.7 uses rigid GAGA and projectivity (after closing up in projective space) to find a vector bundle surjecting onto the ideal sheaf; fibre products of perfectoid spaces over an affinoid field are perfectoid by [KL15, Cor. 3.6.18].

Lemma 5.6: choose open immersions X_i -> V_i^an with V_i projective; for U affinoid perfectoid in X_infty x X_infty, W_i = U x_{V_i^an x V_i^an, Delta} V_i^an is affinoid perfectoid with W_i -> U Zariski closed by Lemma 5.7; the limit over i is a cofiltered limit of Zariski-closed embeddings with fixed target, hence Zariski closed.

nodes.title: Hodge type: the tower of genuine minimal compactifications is perfectoid, analytically separated and a good tower
nodes.statement: Hansen-Johansson Proposition 5.14 and Corollary 5.15: let (G, X) be a Shimura datum of Hodge type with reflex field E and Hodge cocharacter mu, Sh_K(G, X) its canonical model (normal, quasi-projective over E) and Sh*_K(G, X) its normal projective minimal compactification; fix a prime of E over p with completion E_p and let X_K, X*_K be the associated rigid spaces over E_p. For every open compact K^p in G(A_f^p), X*_{K^p} = lim_{K_p} X*,diamond_{K^pK_p} is a perfectoid space; it is analytically separated and has a pair of coverings by finitely many open affinoid perfectoid U_i, V_i with closure of U_i contained in V_i, all pulled back from open affinoids at some finite level. Hence for any cofinal system of open compact K_p in G(Q_p) the tower (X*_{K^pK_p}) is a good tower over E_p (Definition 5.12). Corollary 5.15: for any open compact K in G(A_f) and cofinal K_p, the tower (X*_{K cap K_p}) is a good tower, where K cap K_p means K cap (G(A_f^p)K_p). By construction there is a map X*_{K^p} -> Xbar*_{K^p} to Scholze's image compactification, which need not be an isomorphism.

This map factors through the closed Fl_{G,mu} in Fl_{G~,mu~}, and the resulting pi_HT: S_{K^p} -> Fl_{G,mu} is independent of the choice of embedding of Shimura data. Construction: with G the pointwise stabilizer of tensors (s_alpha) in V^(x) [Del82, Prop. 3.1], the p-adic tensors s_{alpha,p} (defined over E by the argument of Lemma 2.3.2) define the P_mu-torsor P_p on (S_K)_proet of isomorphisms V_p (x) O^ -> V (x) O^ matching s_{alpha,p} with s_alpha and the relative Hodge-Tate filtration with the ascending filtration of mu (Lemma 2.3.6), independent of the embedding (Lemma 2.3.7); the G-torsor G_p obtained by forgetting filtrations has a canonical section over S_{K^p} (the universal trivialization of the Tate module respecting tensors), and P_p gives a G(Q_p)-equivariant G_p -> Fl_{G,mu}, whence pi_HT in Fl_{G,mu}(S_{K^p}) compatible with the Siegel map.

nodes.title: Pre-abelian type and the connected Shimura data (G^der, X^+), (G^ad, X^+) attached to a Shimura datum
nodes.statement: Hansen-Johansson Section 4.1 (Deligne's conventions [Del79], [Mil05]): a Shimura datum (G, X) has attached connected Shimura data (G^der, X^+) and (G^ad, X^+) and the Shimura datum (G^ad, X^ad), for a chosen component X^+ of X. (G, X) is of Hodge type if there is a closed immersion into a Siegel datum, and of abelian type if there are (G_1, X_1) of Hodge type and a central isogeny G_1^der -> G^der inducing (G_1^ad, X_1^+) = (G^ad, X^+). Definition 4.1 (following [Moo98, 2.10]): a connected Shimura datum (G, X) is of pre-abelian type if there is a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G~, X~) with (G^ad, X) = (G~^ad, X~^+); a Shimura datum (G, X) is of pre-abelian type if (G^der, X^+) is. In the proof of Theorem 5.20 one fixes a Hodge-type (G_1, X_1) with a central isogeny G_1^der -> G^ad inducing (G_1^ad, X_1^+) = (G^ad, X^+).
hypotheses: Only an isomorphism of adjoint connected data with a Hodge-type datum is required; no central isogeny to G^der is assumed (this is weaker than abelian type).
Remark 4.2: for semisimple G, G admits a connected Shimura datum iff G has no compact Q-factors and X^G is Hermitian symmetric; the no-compact-factor assumption is kept for simplicity.

Abelian type implies pre-abelian type by composing the isomorphism of adjoint data.

nodes.title: Good towers: stability under finite maps of towers and perfectoidness of finite group quotients commuting with the limit
nodes.statement: Hansen-Johansson Definition 5.12: over a nonarchimedean field K, a good tower is a cofiltered inverse system (X_i) of locally noetherian adic spaces over Spa K such that (1) each X_i is the analytification of a projective variety and the transition maps are finite, (2) X = lim X_i^diamond is a perfectoid space, and (3) X has a pair of coverings by open affinoid perfectoid U_j, V_j with closure(U_j) in V_j, each pulled back from an open affinoid at some finite level. Proposition 5.13: (1) if (Y_i) is a good tower and (X_i) -> (Y_i) is a map of cofiltered systems with finite maps f_i, then (X_i) is a good tower; (2) if (X_i) is a good tower with an action of a finite group G, then the categorical quotient X/G is a perfectoid space and X/G = lim X_i/G. It is not claimed that (X_i/G) is again a good tower.
hypotheses: Finite group G acting compatibly on the tower.

Inputs: Theorem 5.8 (for an analytically separated perfectoid space X over a nonarchimedean field with finite group action such that the closure of every rank one point lies in an open affinoid perfectoid, X/G is perfectoid, the quotient map is affinoid in a weak sense, and X^diamond/G = (X/G)^diamond); Lemma 5.9 (perfectoidness along finite maps of towers); Lemma 5.6 (analytic separatedness); [Sch17, Lemma 11.11] (qcqs maps of spatial diamonds bijective on (C, C+)-points are isomorphisms).

(2), limit comparison: X/G -> lim X_i/G is a qcqs map of spatial diamonds; surjectivity on (C, C+)-points uses nonempty compact inverse limits of the finite fibres W_{i,j}; injectivity uses that the sets G_i of g with g x_i = y_i are nonempty with injective transitions, so lim G_i is nonempty; pro-etale covers of geometric points split, so points of the quotient sheaf are computed naively.
